title: Timing / Execution Verification Promotion Review
canonical_rule: Librarium remains canonical. Runtime/generated data remain consumers and are not sources of independent game truth.

verified_promotions.scope_limit: Architecture only: verifies MajorMUD is a host-managed MajorBBS/Worldgroup module. Does not verify gameplay cadence constants.
verified_promotions.rationale: The repository contains original WCC/WBB MajorMUD module artifacts and docs identifying MajorMUD as hosted under Worldgroup/MajorBBS; MBBSEmu exposes the corresponding module dispatch model.
evidence_chain: ImportedDatabases/WCCDefaultInstall/wcc default/WCCMMUD.DOC identifies WCCMMUD as the Worldgroup/MajorMUD module documentation.
Evidence/CodeUpdate0084_0087/wcc_wbb_binary_timing_symbol_hits_0085.json shows _ljngame_sttrou, _ljngame_stsrou, and _begin_polling symbols in imported module DLLs.
MBBSEmu HostProcess/MbbsHost.cs models host-managed module state dispatch, polling, RTKICK, RTIHDLR, and SYSCYC processing.

verified_promotions.scope_limit: Verifies symbol-level equivalence for the inspected WCC/WBB DLLs only; does not prove binary identity or cadence values.
verified_promotions.rationale: The imported WCC and WBB MajorMUD DLLs both expose the same timing-relevant symbol set in the repository scan.
evidence_chain: Evidence/CodeUpdate0084_0087/wcc_wbb_binary_timing_symbol_hits_0085.json contains 234 timing/gameplay symbol hits across the inspected DLLs.

verified_promotions.scope_limit: Verifies presence of background, autocombat, delay, and cycle-related symbols in original imported DLLs; does not verify their exact cadence or ordering.
verified_promotions.rationale: Both imported DLLs expose MajorMUD-specific background buckets, autocombat routines, delay routines, and system-cycle symbols.
evidence_chain: Evidence/CodeUpdate0084_0087/wcc_wbb_binary_timing_symbol_hits_0085.json records symbol hits in both WCC and WBB DLLs.

corroborated_promotions.scope_limit: Corroborated model: host-driven scheduling is the best supported execution model. Exact Classic order/cadence remains unverified.
corroborated_promotions.rationale: MBBSEmu provides readable host-loop behavior, and WCC/WBB binaries expose module callbacks and scheduler-facing symbols.

corroborated_promotions.scope_limit: Corroborates that MajorMUD interfaces with host delayed scheduling. Seconds semantics are observed in MBBSEmu; original DLL cadence values are still unresolved.
corroborated_promotions.rationale: RTKICK is implemented as host delayed scheduling in MBBSEmu and _rtkick/_my_rtkick are present in both imported MajorMUD DLLs.

not_promoted.reason: The user-provided MegaMUD-style excerpt is relevant, but no original MegaMUD config/source file containing CommandDelay, CombatPulse, or TickSyncBuffer was found in the repository pass. MMUD Explorer also has ROUND_SECS=5 in its model, so the 1.5s claim cannot be promoted.

not_promoted.current_state: Derived / observed for one WCC global-message/page interval
not_promoted.reason: WCC documentation supports a 3-second page/global-message window, but this does not prove HP/mana/spell/recovery tick cadence.
Tick clipping follows logically from a global decrement model, but no primary documentation or runtime trace proves the behavior.
Symbols exist in WCC/WBB DLLs, but cadence constants and callers need disassembly/runtime trace evidence.
Host/session architecture implies output is host mediated, but exact original flushing granularity is not proven.

next_work: Disassemble/cross-reference _majormud_syscyc and _background_* to recover cadence constants.
Cross-reference _do_autocombat/_restart_autocombat/_add_delay to determine combat scheduling values.
Locate original MegaMUD timing configuration/source provenance or remove the 1500ms claim from promotion candidates.
Use runtime traces to validate whether 3-second global-message interval also maps to regen/spell ticks.
